Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431176




Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Meditation and Prayer lesson audio Then Practice often.

2. Spend time in meditation and practicing prayer.

3. You may find it helpful to identify and write out your resistance to these
two practices.



Some notes

When you express differently, or do anything differently you build new neural
pathways. Your consciousness also grows and expands. You open yourself to new
perceptions and experiences. You are changing your sense of self, and your sense of
relationship to the world around you.

By practicing being in a state of calm, quiet mind, love, and peace, your brain operates
at different frequencies. Most of the day people are concerned with getting things done.
They are in a state of low level stress. They frequency in their brain is in the low-beta
range. When you relax or sleep, you move into alpha and delta wavelength. When the
 beta brain waves, which is the activity in the pre-frontal cortex turns off, your mind is
quiet and relaxed. You are turning of the stress of the internal chatter.

Different things happen in your brain and in your body in those relaxed states. Your
nervous system moves out of the survival patterns and rests. This allows your cells and
organs in your body to go into a recharge recover state. They get to rest too. This can
help with digestion, sleep, inflammation, long term pains, and auto-immune issues.

Taking the time to calm your mind will calm and change your emotional state. This
changes your nervous system which then changes the signals the cells in your body are
getting. Meditation is a whole body benefit exercise.

I suggest you make this a regular practice, at least for a month. It is time enough to build
a new habit, make it enjoyable, and build new neural pathways that are lasting. With
neural pathways built, it won’t be like work to go sit.

To make it a routine, sit in the same place, at the same time, if possible. If it is in the
morning, and you don’t make time for it then, then meditate in the evening or afternoon
                                                                                                                                   1/2

that day. Approach it like exercise, except for your mind, attention, and emotions. If you
miss your regular time slot it is better to fit it in at a different time than to put it off til
tomorrow.

You may want a place that is quiet with as little distraction as possible. This might mean
sitting in a park, or in nature. For some people it might be in their car in their
driveway.

It doesn’t have to look spiritual.

Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431177

The old neural pathways aren’t being used if you are creating and using new ones.
When they aren’t being used they wither. That withering is like a death. Those old
circuits might be dying and it might feel sad, grief, fear of death, or like something is
starving.

The releasing emotions practice from session 9 may come in useful.

If your body is uncomfortable and you have a difficult time sitting, then sit in a
comfortable chair. Personally, my body doesn’t do well in the cross-legged position on
the floor, so I often sit in a comfortable chair, or cross legged on a couch. I also like to
have back support. If I can make my body comfortable then I focus better on the
breathing and emotions. Get over the resistance about the body by making it
comfortable.

The sitting doesn’t have to be torture to the body. If it is, then change it.

If you don’t like the words, then change them. Some people will have a reaction to the
world “prayer” or “god” etc. Make an expression that you like and that feels good to
you. You don’t have to do meditation or your prayer the way someone else does.
Meditation and prayer is about liberating your consciousness, emotions, spirit, and your
voice. This isn’t about trapping your expression into someone else’s words.

Singing can be your meditation. Sing a song you love, you enjoy. Sing something that
opens your heart with joy. Singing isn’t my kind of meditation and communion but it
can be yours.

This open expression of love is definitely not about “dogma”. One of the biggest
objections to spiritual/religious practices is all the “dogma” and rules. There are not
rules about what your meditation and prayer practice is.

There is guidance. That guidance is that it be enjoyable and that you practice regularly.

Common Questions

   selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-common-questions-6431178

What should I be accomplishing in meditation?

It depends. Sometimes it takes a whole lot of will power to just sit still and not move.
This can be an accomplishment.

If you are sitting still, and the voices are loud, the body is uncomfortable, and
unpleasant emotions are churning, then that might be a good process.

You were able to sit still through a storm where your ego is trying to drive you away
from calm and peace. You exercised your will and attention and didn’t let it succumb to
the ego. You didn’t let the voices in your head drive you away from practicing. You may
not realize it very clearly, but you were in a different state of mind than those voices.
You might not have felt good, because you were feeling all the emotions from the
resisting voices. But you were in a different point of view. Next time it will feel and look
different.

It’s not pleasant, but it will reap huge benefits over time. It will also get easier. Then
there will be moments or days when a breakthrough happens.



How long and often should I meditate or pray?

Work on doing as much as you did yesterday, plus a little more.

Singing a song can be 4 minutes, and completely change your state. If you sing it 3
times, you have more benefit. But maybe if you sing it 9 time you become bored and it is
feeling wrote and empty. Or maybe even like an obligation. If this is the case then you
are singing the song too much.

It will vary, and you will grow muscles, focus, and confidence over time. Early on 20-30
minutes was a long time for me. If I was listening to a guided meditation, then I could
go longer with out losing focus.

Years later meditations can take you much deeper, or further out into consciousness,
depending on how you imagine it. In those times it might take 20-30 min to get into the
groove of the meditation.



Is it okay to use an meditation app for guidance?



                                                                                                                                   1/2

Yes, use whatever support materials that help. Remember the intent is about cultivating
and expressing those good emotions.

When you are learning props, or crutches will help you move forward. Later, your
muscles will be stronger and you can put the props and crutches aside and run.



What should a good meditation session look like?

It will change all the time. I’ve never had two meditations that went the same. I couldn’t
make them the same if I tried.

Try it for yourself and see what happens.

In my experience you are not the only factor in your meditation. There are other
consciousnesses, forces, and emotions there. You may find yourself inter-playing with
them.

It may help to approach meditation with curiosity and adventure.

Sometimes you may sit to meditate with plans for a really loving process. Except when
you sit for a few minutes you discover a lot of anger. Then you spend the next 30
minutes releasing the emotions of anger. That can be a good meditation.
